beats.narration_text: Last week, Gavia learned to listen. This is Sai. This week, it learned a new subject: Veg Net, a model for four invasive lake plants. How good is it? And does it know a native plant when it sees one? We showed it forty of them.

show.event: the ask types in under 'Hello, Sai'
three result lines land
'native look-alikes: 25 of 40 boxed' lands last and holds

props.command: Gavia 0.5.0 adds Vegnet, a model for four invasive lake plants. How accurate is it, and does it mistake native look-alikes for invasives? Test it on natives.

beats.narration_text: Here's the change, on a stand of purple loosestrife: the box names the species, at ninety-seven percent. Check an image now has a Model menu. Loon Net looks for loons. Veg Net looks for purple loosestrife, common reed, water chestnut and yellow flag iris. It's the model slot we pointed to two weeks ago, with a second model in it.

beats.narration_text: Veg Net's headline number is a mean average precision of zero point seven two. A box counts as a hit when its intersection over union with the reviewed box is at least one half. Each species gets an average precision, and the four are averaged. Water chestnut scores zero point nine six. Purple loosestrife, zero point five four. One mean, a wide spread.

show.event: what counts as a hit: IoU ≥ 0.5
mAP: the mean of four per-species APs
the four numbers average to 0.720

props.title: What “mean AP@0.5 = 0.72” is made of
props.note: One mean; a spread from 0.536 to 0.959.
props.conditions: A: Vegnet's box · B: the reviewed label box · AP₁…AP₄: each species' area under its precision–recall curve · 28 val photos, 32 stands · Gavia v0.5.0 examples/evaluate.rs, re-run 9 Nov 2026

beats.narration_text: Meet the four. Water chestnut, with its floating rosettes. Common reed, the introduced frag-MY-teez. Yellow flag iris. And purple loosestrife, with its magenta spikes, the one Veg Net finds hardest. Each was trained on twenty-six photos and checked on seven, with boxes drafted by another model and reviewed by a person.

common reed, 0.80
yellow flag iris, 0.59
purple loosestrife, 0.54

beats.narration_text: So we asked it about natives. On its own invasive photos, Veg Net draws a box on twenty-five of twenty-eight. On forty iNaturalist photos of native look-alikes, it boxed twenty-five. Five of eight native American reeds. Seven of eight watershields. The rest were fireweed, blue vervain and blue flag iris, and not one of the forty is invasive.

show.event: its own invasive photos: 25 of 28
native look-alikes: 25 of 40
American reed 5 of 8, watershield 7 of 8

props.title: Photos Vegnet puts an invasive-plant box on
props.note: Gavia v0.5.0 Detector, veg_v1, the app's 0.25 threshold · 40 research-grade iNaturalist photos, 8 each of 5 natives · evidence/lookalike_check.rs, 9 Nov 2026

beats.narration_text: In the app, it looks like this. Native fireweed: purple loosestrife, ninety-seven percent. Native watershield: water chestnut, ninety-five. Native American reed: common reed, ninety-eight. It's the eider from two weeks ago, the one the loon model called two loons. Every one of Veg Net's hundred and thirty-two photos had an invasive in it, so it never learned what native looks like.

watershield boxed as water chestnut, 95%
American reed boxed as common reed, 98%

beats.narration_text: Gavia's own roadmap already names the fixes. Boxes checked by hand, not drafted. Many more photos per species. Native look-alikes in the training set, so the model learns what no looks like. Submerged invaders, like Eurasian watermilfoil. And the place and date of each photo, exported for mapping. Twenty-five of forty is now the number to beat.

show.event: hand-checked boxes and more photos land
native look-alikes and submerged species land
GPS, date and export close the grid

beats.narration_text: So: the same offline app now looks for invasive plants as well as loons. Veg Net finds water chestnut well and purple loosestrife poorly, and it boxed twenty-five of forty native look-alikes. Until it has seen natives, treat each box as a lead for someone who knows plants.

the score and look-alike lines fill in
'Next, by its own roadmap' closes it

artifactLines: Gavia's Model menu now switches between loons and four invasive lake plants, all offline.
Vegnet's mean AP@0.5 is 0.720 on 28 val photos: 0.959 for water chestnut, 0.536 for purple loosestrife.
It boxed 25 of 40 photos of native look-alikes; every training photo held an invasive.
Next, by its own roadmap: hand-checked boxes, native look-alikes, submerged species.
